newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares seen higher, looking to Wall St.
newsitem.headline: German shares seen higher, looking to Wall St.

text.p: German shares were expected to climb and could make new record highs on Thursday, dealers said, although that will depend on how Wall Street performs overnight, as it digests the results of the U.S. election.

The IBIS DAX, which measures all-day computer trade in the DAX index of 30 leading shares, rose to a day high of 2,737.13 up 20.97 marks, or 0.77 in late dealings, after Wall Street opened stronger and German Bunds rose.
The IBIS DAX could have tested its high of 2,745.82 points had it not been held back by heavy losses by Siemens, down after its bearish outlook for the 1996/97 financial year.
Siemens lost over nine percent at one stage, pulling the rest of the index down, then recovered slightly to trade down 6.92 marks at 73.05 marks. Over 11 million Siemens shares changed hands.
Meanwhile Hoechst was also heavily traded, rising 2.36 marks, or over four percent, at 60.70 marks, after the firm's nine-month results were well received.
Competing chemical companies BASF AG and Bayer AG were pulled up by Hoechst's success. BASF were up 75 pfennigs at 51.25 marks in IBIS dealings, while Bayer climbed 88 pfennigs to 58.82 marks.
Preference shares in business software group SAP AG gained the most ground, continuing to recover from the blow of a profit warning two weeks ago. over five percent, or 10.70 marks, at 208.20.

Industrial group Daimler Benz AG also climbed strongly, after a newsletter said the firm was due to report nine-month turnover growth of 10 percent on Thursday. Daimler ended IBIS trade up 1.64 marks at 92.69 marks.
